distractors.reason: 'Quickly' describes speed of movement. 'Wake up quickly' does not describe the time you wake up, so we use 'early' instead.
'Soon' means in a short time from now. 'Wake up soon' does not say whether it is early or late in the day.
'Fast' describes speed. We do not say 'wake up fast' to talk about the time of day.

example_sentence: Please wake up ___ tomorrow, because we have a meeting.
l1_interference: Los hispanohablantes pueden colocar el adverbio antes del verbo y decir 'early wake up', por la flexibilidad del orden de palabras en español. En inglés el adverbio va después de 'wake up': 'wake up early'.
explanation: In English, 'wake up' is a phrasal verb, and the adverb 'early' comes after it to say when the action happens. 'Early' tells the time, so it is the natural partner of 'wake up'.

related_collocations.example: I always go to bed early on school nights.
Sorry I arrive late, the bus was slow.
We can finish early if we work together.

memory_tip: The adverb goes at the END of the phrasal verb: wake up + EARLY. Think 'wake up, then early = the time'.
